notes: Circuit follows the image: 5V -> rail(+) -> button side 1 (column 4); button side 2 (column 6) -> pin 2 and via 10k pull-down to GND rail.
Pushbutton legs straddle the centre gap in columns 4 and 6; the two legs in the same column are one side (1.l/1.r in column 4, 2.l/2.r in column 6).
Catalogue bank 't' (rows a-e) is taken as the half nearest the power rails the wires use, so rails are named tp/tn; exact rail hole numbers are arbitrary (each rail is one strip).
Resistor right lead assumed in column 9 (same column as the black wire to the GND rail); exact rows are approximate from the image.
The built-in LED on pin 13 is on the Uno; no external LED is used by this tutorial.

The circuit image shows no breadboard; the parts list names 2 mini breadboards. I used one breadboard (bb1) only as the junction for the two 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors and the I2C lines. Mini breadboards are not in the catalogue, so I used the catalogue breadboard type.

The image shows the two I2C lines and the 3V line sharing nodes with the resistors, with no wire drawn between the boards' A4 pins. I therefore routed A4 (SDA) and A5 (SCL) from both boards to a shared breadboard column each.
Each pull-up resistor goes from its I2C line to 3V3 from the reader board. 3V3 is distributed over the breadboard top power rail (tp), so tp.1, tp.2 and tp.3 are one strip.
Boards are 3.3 V logic, so the pull-ups go to 3V3 and not 5 V.
The manual calls A4 SDA and A5 SCL (the text says SDA on A4 and SCL on A5). The graph connects A4 to A4 and A5 to A5.
The two USB cables go to the computer for power and serial. The computer is not modelled.
The Arduino Nano 33 IoT is new to the catalogue. The 3V pin in the diagram is named 3V3.
The built-in LED is on the reader board and needs no external parts. No external LED circuit is listed.
Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention (rows f-j = bank 'b'); the image's upper half (rows f-j) is therefore bank 'b'. Rail hole numbers are approximate positions read from the image.
Photoresistor (5V side) and 10k resistor (GND side) form a voltage divider whose junction (column 10) goes to A0 by the yellow wire.
LED anode (bent leg, column 22) is fed from pin 9 via the blue wire; cathode (column 23) goes through the 220 ohm resistor to the GND rail, matching the schematic (series resistor).
The text mentions 'Analog input 2' in the circuit caption, but the text and images use A0, so A0 is used.
Top breadboard rail nearest the edge (black line) is treated as ground 'tn'; the red-line rail is 5V 'tp'.

Fix for the V4 port-reuse error: the black ground jumpers (wire5, wire7) shared a hole with a resistor leg. Each now sits in its own hole in the same column strip (13b.i and 26b.i), so they are still electrically connected to the resistor leg in 13b.h / 26b.g's strip. The image shows these wires in the same columns as the resistor ends, so this does not change the circuit.
